title: Horizontal pasting for fixed normalized proper/open comparisons
statement: Let Lambda be a finite commutative ring. Use bounded-below derived etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], exact open extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], proper maps [def-weil-proper-morphism] and open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every commutative proper/open square fix ordinary natural isomorphisms delta:i_!r_*≅p_*k_! and derived natural isomorphisms gamma:i_!Rr_*≅Rp_*k_!. Assume that for each square k:A→B, i:C→D, r:A→C, p:B→D with k p=r i, delta_F followed by p_*(k_!F→k_*F) and the compositor k_*p_*→(k p)_* equals i_!r_*F→i_*r_*F followed by the compositor r_*i_*→(k p)_*. Assume also that gamma.hom is exactly rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange(delta.hom). Then gamma obeys horizontal pasting, with the extensionZeroCompDerivedPlusIso compositors [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. The equation, with all compositors and orientations, is specified verbatim in the Lean record. Only equalities of these fixed maps are concluded; this statement neither constructs the comparison isomorphisms nor asserts their identity or refinement/base-change laws.

proof.text:
Write $h=ir=pk$. Proper maps are separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion, and locally on that open subscheme its ring map is the identity, a finite-type map. Thus the separated and locally finite-type hypotheses of [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] hold. That node gives, for every module sheaf $F$ on $A$, the canonical identification
$$\delta_Q(F):i_!r_*F=i_!^{\mathrm{supp}}r_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=h_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=p_!^{\mathrm{supp}}k_!^{\mathrm{supp}}F=p_*k_!F.$$
All the equalities mean the same subsheaf of $h_*F$: a section is carried to the same section, rather than to an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Thus $\delta_Q$ is natural and $\Lambda$-linear, and extends degreewise to complexes. For horizontally adjacent squares, all identifications of the underlying sheaves are identities on these common sections. Hence the ordinary horizontal composition equation holds. The proper-support composition result applies without Cartesian or quasi-compact-open assumptions.

proof.text:
For horizontal composition choose bounded-below injective $J$ on the left, $t:k_!J\to I$ in the middle, and $v:l_!I\to L$ on the right. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $w=v\circ l_!t:l_!k_!J\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The two-square comparison is represented by
$$j_!i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{j_!(p_*t\circ\delta_{Q_1})}j_!p_*I\xrightarrow{q_*v\circ\delta_{Q_2}}q_*L.$$
Naturality of the sheaf identification $\delta_{Q_2}$ moves $t$ through it. The sheaf composition equality in step 1 then makes this map $q_*w\circ\delta_{Q_2Q_1}$, the representative for the outer rectangle. The identification $j_!i_!\cong(ji)_!$ is the sheaf support-composition equality in [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], applied degreewise; its exactness just cited lets it descend to $D^+$. This proves the stated horizontal equation.
